status: REGISTERED before implementation and data collection
question: With the actor restricted to screen-observable body features, does a critic that sees privileged simulator state learn faster at equal wall-clock budget than a critic restricted to the actor's own inputs, and does the resulting actor deploy better?
hypothesis: Asymmetric training (privileged critic, restricted actor) improves equal-budget learning speed without leaking privileged information into actor inference; deployment quality is measured on the same restricted observations.
actor_inputs: the restricted screen-body vector: 8 body features and 8 validity masks over a 4-frame history (64 inputs) from the analytic projection used by the screen-body student; identical in both arms; no privileged feature enters the actor at training or inference

arms.restricted_critic: critic input equals the actor input (64 values)
arms.privileged_critic: critic input is the full 96-value idealized simulator observation (4-frame stack of the 24 features); actor unchanged

training.algorithm: PPO original-0.1.0 with a separated critic input path

evaluation.observation_at_evaluation: restricted actor observations only; the critic is not used
evaluation.leak_check: the actor network's input dimension is asserted to be 64 and its forward pass is executed on restricted observations only; a test fails if privileged features can reach the actor

success_criteria: the privileged-critic arm attains higher validation distance at 300 s and 600 s in all three seeds with a positive paired difference; otherwise report no benefit
relation_to_cycle_1: Cycle 1 oracle PPO trained both actor and critic on idealized state and is not this experiment

cycle2_versions.observation_schema: screen-body-restricted-64 (actor) with critic input recorded per arm
